conclusion: We propose that to be real is to have closed: that reality is not a substance, a substrate, or a set, but a ledger of survived closures. A thing is real when it is a package that earned its objecthood through audited gates and pays, continuously, to keep it. The proposal is grounded in the Six Birds corpus, which has spent the last years doing something Nietzsche predicted and no one else has attempted: worshipping the stone. The corpus constructs geometry, logic, time, probability, objects, events, agents, institutions, and selves from bare substrates, under explicit audit, with every failure banked and every success priced. The method of this paper is an itemized metaphysics. Every claim is either free, a theorem of the corpus at its stated grade, or purchased, spending one of two named axioms: Ontic Closure Completeness and Substrate Indifference. On this basis we argue that the Born rule's shape is the generic fate of compressed record layers, so that probability is born at the lens; that a simulation which passes a closure's gates is not a simulation of the thing but an instance of it, which is why lattice QCD computes the true proton; that ``matter'' and ``information'' are altitude labels, so that an economy is literally a ghost made of people; that mathematics is closure engineering in vitro, the design of lawful theory extensions ahead of any run, and in practice a map that unfolds only where someone walks; that the explanatory gap of consciousness is a non-descent certificate, predicted rather than embarrassing; that life and intelligence are graded, auditable positions on real axes rather than binaries; that a civilization which learns this grammar crosses into the era of meta-emergence, where creation itself is a wielded power, and that peace is a closure state, an achievement that strengthens rather than dissolves the identities it comprises; and that the great paradoxes (sorites, Theseus, Zeno, Mary's room, the unreasonable effectiveness of mathematics, the arrow of time) dissolve under ledger discipline, most of them because they demanded of a layer a certificate that no layer can issue. We close eight old problems and open eight new ones. The last sacrifice is Sacrifice itself.

conclusion: Enumerating nearly twelve thousand chiral gauge structures token-blind, the closure chain forces a thin skeleton: the Standard Model's gauge algebra (conditional on one separation condition), ^2 _W = 3/8 at the embedding point, exact proton stability.
expanded_source_wording_tex: \textbf{The thin forced skeleton.} Necessity and contingency, in physics, stop being moods and become computed columns. Enumerating nearly twelve thousand chiral gauge structures token-blind, the closure chain forces a thin skeleton: the Standard Model's gauge algebra (conditional on one separation condition), $\sin^2\theta_W = 3/8$ at the embedding point, exact proton stability. And it proves other quantities invisible to in-layer law: the generation count, the electroweak scale, the value of the cosmological constant. ``The Standard Model, on this evidence, is not one derivable object. It is a \emph{selection} with a thin forced skeleton --- and the calculus proves both the skeleton and the thinness.'' The laws of nature, like the axioms of set theory \citep{zfc}, factor into a free column and a purchased column. That physics and mathematics have the same receipt structure is the one-grammar thesis in its most compact form.

expanded_source_wording_tex: \textbf{The physical kind.} In this grammar a singularity is where a layer confesses its budget: a needle the native probes cannot dissolve, a Zeno cascade of the multiscale frontier \citep{ns}, a closure failure at the chart's edge. Some singularities are chart artifacts, like the phantom-crossing pattern of \S\ref{sec:grammar}: redraw the lens and audit what survives. Some are genuine boundaries, and there the honest physics is not ``infinite curvature'' but ``this closure's claims end here; a strict extension is licensed.'' A black hole's interior, read this way, is a nonclaim boundary drawn by nature. The information paradox has already been reclassified on the corpus's carriers as ``a property of the readout, not of the carrier'' \citep{threestones}. Where the ledger cannot follow, the correct entry is not infinity; it is \emph{out of scope, pending extension}. That, notice, is also what the ledger says about tomorrow.

conclusion: Read philosophically: why is there something rather than nothing is, in this grammar, a well-typed open problem.
expanded_source_wording_tex: \textbf{4. Can nothing close?} Foundations~IV explicitly defers ``stability of nothing'' for want of a recognition source. Read philosophically: \emph{why is there something rather than nothing} is, in this grammar, a well-typed open problem. Does the null package survive audit? If nothing fails to close (no carrier, no records, no persistence conditions: nothing cannot \emph{keep} being nothing), then something is what that failure looks like. We flag this as the purest Tier-O speculation in the paper. But no other tradition has given the oldest question a form, as opposed to an answer or a shrug.

conclusion: What happens to a civilization after the crossing is an open question, the ninth of this book, and we will not pretend to close it.
expanded_source_wording_tex: What happens to a civilization after the crossing is an open question, the ninth of this book, and we will not pretend to close it. But the grammar constrains the answer's shape. Wielded creation accelerates enablement-time: more strict extensions per generation, more ghosts above and more below. And the corpus's bounded-reflexivity law holds that audit capacity does not scale for free \citep{cognition}. So the era of meta-emergence poses one structural alternative, the same alternative \S\ref{sec:singularities} posed for machine minds, now at the scale of the species: \textbf{either coherence grows with creative power, or the civilization's own creations outrun its audits} and it becomes substrate to ghosts it can no longer read. A civilization past the threshold must evolve toward higher and tighter closure: wider common quotients, faster certificate flow, denser repair transport. Not as moral aspiration. As a viability condition, of the same standing as any other gate.
